text:
Linus Karlsson wears an A in Vancouver, and on the Canucks Insider Podcast this week he talked about "What It Means to Be an Assistant Captain." Canucks Army's headline says he "believes he has another level to find," and Daily Hive called him "an underrated beast" the night Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis watched him set up a tying goal in Edmonton without a point to show for it: a "Big reverse hit on Nugent-Hopkins to hold possession, great zone entry."

The box score hasn't kept up lately: 10 points in 21 games, only 2 in his last ten, against about 5.2 our numbers expected. His finishing is close to his chances (4 goals on 4.7 expected goals), and his ice time is up about a minute over that stretch. The case for him is in the details. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play last season (his team created 0.17 more expected goals per 60 with him on, 86th percentile among forwards) while skating with teammates in the bottom 3%. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found him getting 6.7 chances per 60 from the home-plate area in front of the net, 88th percentile.
headline: Linus Karlsson does the work around the points
